title: The Vault page, from route to per-secret custody
summary: The `/vault` route is a one-line shim onto `VaultPanel`, a client component that renders entirely from the app shell's vault state. It shows the seal lamp (locked/unlocked) and the key source (OS keychain vs passphrase), gates the whole register behind an unlock, offers an empty-state add-value affordance, and draws each stored secret as a masked-until-revealed lifecycle row. Nothing here fetches directly — the shell has already pulled `/api/vault/secrets`, and the unlock button posts `/api/vault/unlock`.

states.label: Vault
states.description: The drillbook asks that this page communicate security state and empty-state actions clearly, and keep its lifecycle table and controls readable and contained. It is the `/vault` route, and the whole page renders from one client component reading the app shell's vault state.

steps.title: The route is a one-line shim onto VaultPanel
steps.description: Navigating to `/vault` lands on a server component that does nothing but mount `VaultPanel`. There is no data-loading in the route itself — the panel is a client component that reads everything it needs from the shell context — so the route file is five lines long.

steps.title: The seal panel reads state and key source from the shell
steps.description: `VaultPanel` pulls `vaultUnlocked` and `vaultKeySource` out of `useAppShell()` and renders the security state directly: the lamp goes live and the heading flips to "Vault ready" only when unlocked, and the ledger prints `unlocked`/`locked`, the key source (`OS keychain` by default, or a passphrase source) and the fixed `AES-256-GCM` cipher. `vaultUnlocked` is the one boolean that decides the whole page below.

steps.title: The primary action is gated on the seal
steps.description: When the vault is sealed the panel shows one button — "Unlock from keychain" — which asks the OS keychain for the master key by calling `unlockVault("")`; it disables and reads "Requesting key…" while `busy === "vault"`. Once unlocked the button is replaced by a static "Ready for scoped delivery" mark, so the operator never sees an unlock control for a vault that is already open.

steps.title: The register has two empty states plus an add-value affordance
steps.description: The secret register distinguishes "sealed" from "empty": while locked (or awaiting a passphrase) it shows a "Register sealed" prompt and no names; unlocked but with zero secrets it shows "No stored values" and invites an add. The "Add value" button (disabled until unlocked) pushes a fresh blank row into `secrets`, which then renders as a `SecretRow`.

steps.title: Each secret is a masked-until-revealed lifecycle row
steps.description: A `SecretRow` never holds plaintext until the operator asks for it: `held` is true only once `secret.value` is a string (revealed or typed), so the value field stays empty and shows the server's non-reconstructable preview as a placeholder. The reveal button is disabled once `held` (or for a never-set row) and fetches exactly one plaintext value on click — the mechanism that keeps a page load from ever surfacing a credential.

steps.title: The seal state and secrets come from the shell's API calls
steps.description: VaultPanel itself makes no fetches — the app shell does. On load `refreshAll()` pulls `/api/vault/secrets` (masks only, never plaintext) alongside the library and compositions; the "Unlock from keychain" button posts `/api/vault/unlock` and updates `vaultUnlocked`/`vaultNeedsPassword`/`secrets` from the response; and a per-row reveal posts `/api/vault/secrets/reveal` for exactly one plaintext value, recorded server-side in the audit log.
steps.note: Endpoints live in src/components/chrome/AppShell.tsx: refreshAll() fetches /api/vault/secrets; unlockVault() posts /api/vault/unlock; revealSecret() posts /api/vault/secrets/reveal.
